prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks That Could Beat the S&P 500

Picking stocks that beat the S&P 500 over one year is hard. In a typical year, most professional large-cap fund managers fail to do it, and about 85–90% trail the index over 10–15 years (S&P's SPIVA reports). A 10-stock portfolio will differ a lot from the index, so it could beat it handily or lag it badly. Also, my knowledge only runs through mid-2026 and I don't have live market data, so **check current prices, valuations and news before buying.**

This list is built around durable themes, with some spread beyond AI:

| # | Company (Ticker) | Why it could outperform | Key risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes most of the world's leading-edge AI chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and others, and has strong pricing power. It's *not* in the S&P 500, so it differentiates your portfolio. | Taiwan geopolitics, tariffs |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers, AI networking, and steady VMware software cash flow | High valuation, reliance on a few big customers |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS growth from AI demand, plus retail margins expanding through advertising and logistics efficiency | Heavy capital spending, consumer slowdown |
| 4 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and grid equipment benefit from surging electricity demand from data centers, with a multi-year backlog | Already priced for strong execution |
| 5 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in obesity and diabetes drugs (Mounjaro/Zepbound), with an oral obesity pill (orforglipron) as a next catalyst | Drug-pricing pressure, high expectations |
| 6 | **Intuitive Surgical (ISRG)** | Dominant in surgical robotics, with recurring revenue from instruments and service | Expensive, rising competition |
| 7 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-in-class bank that benefits from deregulation and dealmaking activity | Credit losses in a recession |
| 8 | **Visa (V)** | Takes a cut of global card spending, with very high margins and steady buybacks | Regulation of card fees, alternative payment methods |
| 9 | **Uber (UBER)** | Now solidly profitable with strong cash flow, and could become the main marketplace for robotaxi fleets | Robotaxi operators could bypass it |
| 10 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Acts as ballast: a large cash pile and a tendency to hold up in selloffs, which is often when outperformance is earned | Lags in strong bull markets; leadership transition after Buffett |

## Things to consider before buying
- **Your biggest single bet is AI spending.** Four names (TSM, AVGO, AMZN, GEV) depend heavily on it. If AI investment cools, this portfolio will probably lag the index.
- **Overlap with the index:** Several of these (AMZN, AVGO, JPM, V, LLY, BRK.B) are already large S&P 500 holdings. They reduce your risk of badly trailing the index, but they also limit how far you can pull ahead of it.
- **Consider a core-satellite approach:** Put 70–80% in an S&P 500 index fund and 20–30% in your picks. This limits the damage if your picks disappoint.
- **Position sizing:** Equal-weighting at about 10% each and rebalancing periodically keeps any one stock from dominating.
- **Set exit rules in advance**, such as selling if the reason you bought no longer holds. Also check how holding periods affect your taxes where you live.

This isn't personalized financial advice. If meaningful money is involved, a licensed advisor can account for your full situation.

I can tailor the list to your risk tolerance, preferred sectors, or what you already own. I can also write a small script to track these picks against SPY over the year.
